SLIDE 1 OF 7

MARS: OUTPOST ZERO

Team: Guardians of the Galaxy 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge

A browser-based educational game where you manage a Mars outpost for 30 Sols — balancing power, water, food and oxygen.

Built around NASA's real challenge: how do you keep people alive when every resource is scarce and every decision has delayed consequences?

SLIDE 2 OF 7 — THE CHALLENGE

Pick Your Astronaut

8 occupations · 3 mission sites · no login needed

Each occupation changes your starting attributes and adds a unique passive ability (e.g. Botanist boosts food production every Sol; Engineer slows system wear).

Mission sites range from the Moon (Moderate) to Deep-Space (Extreme, no resupply).

SLIDE 3 OF 7 — HOW IT WORKS

One Decision Per Sol

Per-Sol flow · real-time status · shortage warnings

Each Sol you pick one action — from routine operations to resource allocation — and end the day. The simulation engine applies production, consumption and radiation. Shortage warnings appear before they become critical.

SLIDE 4 OF 7 — CRISES

Real Consequences

50+ events · delayed effects · power blackout rule

Solar storms, power instability, water contamination — crises fire when conditions match. Choices have immediate and delayed effects (a temporary bypass today causes generator deterioration 2 Sols later). Three consecutive blackout Sols end the mission.

SLIDE 5 OF 7 — RESOURCE ENGINE

No Guesswork

Produced · Used by crew · Net change · Will last

Every room shows where the numbers come from. The engine splits power consumption by consumer (life support, food systems, equipment, emergency systems) so the player understands trade-offs — not just totals.

SLIDE 6 OF 7 — MISSION DEBRIEF

What Happened and Why

Score · 30 decisions · NASA-linked lessons

The debrief shows outcome, score, final resources and crew condition. The decision timeline links every consequence back to the choice that caused it. Each event type opens a lesson grounded in real NASA and ESA sources.

SLIDE 7 OF 7 — THE LEARNING

Decisions Leave Traces

10 educational topics · 20 live NASA/ESA references

CONSEQUENCE rows on the timeline show how past choices ripple forward — matching how NASA engineers think about risk, redundancy and cascading failures. Players finish a run understanding resource scarcity, shielding, life support and decision-making under uncertainty.
